Subject: Exploring a lightweight SDK integration pilot with Redwood

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking a quick call yesterday. BridgeFoundry builds a developer-first orchestration SDK that helps ISVs instrument prompts, trace calls, and standardize schema outputs across multiple model backends. We think Redwood's serving and routing primitives would be a strong strategic match for a joint POC — our customers ask for predictable latencies and vendor routing.

High-level ask: would Redwood be open to a 6-week technical pilot where we: 
- add a Redwood runtime adapter to our SDK (trace hooks + token attribution)
- run a small sandbox with 2 joint customers (non-production)
- evaluate latency/cost delta and telemetry fidelity

I've attached a short MoU and a proposed pilot scope sheet. If this looks interesting, can we lock a 30–45m scoping call next week? Ava (cc'd) handles integrations for us and will join.

Best,
Ethan
Founder, BridgeFoundry

Hi Ethan / Ava,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. I'm available next week on Tue/Wed afternoons EST for a 45m scoping session. Proposed agenda:

1) Goals & success criteria (latency delta threshold, telemetry completeness)
2) Pilot architecture & roles (hosted sandbox vs dedicated dev cluster)
3) Data/security guardrails (no customer PII, RBAC for logs)
4) Timeline & gating (SOW, account approvals, runbook)

Technical notes for Markus: we'll want to confirm one Redwood-serving variant (gpt-like open model) + a fallback cheaper variant. For token-level attribution we'll need an SDK hook that annotates requests with partner_id and prompt_set_id; our runtime can accept X-Redwood-Meta headers.

Attached a one-page pilot checklist and a proposed timeline. Two asks from our side before the call:
- confirm non-prod customers for the sandbox (we'd like at least one SaaS user and one consultancy)
- confirm BridgeFoundry's SLA expectations for the pilot (uptime, telemetry sample rate)

Best,
